changeability.rationale: Nearly every rule (humanization, dashes, sprites, stat labels, sort columns) has one obvious home. The one dent: card construction is duplicated between cardsFor and loadList, so a fix to how a card's sprite/name is derived (exactly the Deoxys-class bug) must be applied in both places, and the home page would silently keep the old behaviour if only cardsFor were fixed.

coupling.rationale: Server and client are separated by a hard, typed seam: raw PokeAPI shapes are transformed into view models in one server module, and every component is a dumb function of those models. The only reach into framework internals is the underscore-prefixed match field in the root head, which is isolated and commented.

app/src/lib/pokedex.server.ts:137 — cardsFor is a real shared abstraction: all three detail pages build card lists through it
app/src/lib/pokedex.server.ts:57-77 — english/latestFlavorText/englishEffect are reusable extraction helpers shared by move/ability/species loaders

app/src/lib/pokedex.server.ts:168-173 — loadList re-inlines card construction instead of reusing a card factory, the one copy-paste seam
abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions track the app's actual variation (cards, sections, type badges, move tables, name/effect extraction) and would stretch to an Items section with little friction. What keeps it from a 5: loadList duplicates the card-mapping idiom instead of sharing a factory with cardsFor, and the three per-resource loaders (loadMove/loadAbility/loadType) are parallel bespoke functions, so a new resource is a template copy rather than a configuration.

findings.issue: Card construction (sprite URL + humanized label + id) is duplicated: cardsFor builds cards from Pokémon refs while loadList builds them inline from species; a change to the card derivation rule (e.g. default-Pokémon sprite for Deoxys-like species) must be made twice, and the home page can drift from the detail pages.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared card factory (e.g. toCard(species, extras)) used by both loadList and cardsFor, so every Pokémon card in the app derives its sprite/name through one code path.

findings.issue: The not-found title check reads the underscore-prefixed router-internal field `m._notFound` and the match `status` string, which may break across TanStack Router upgrades.
findings.suggestion: Prefer framework-supported hooks (e.g. a not-found head override via the root's notFoundComponent companion or rendering the title from the NotFound component's route match) or at least pin and re-verify on upgrades.

findings.issue: The Moves select and the ~90-line SortableMoveTable machinery live inside the Pokémon route file; a second sortable table elsewhere would force an extraction rather than a reuse.
findings.suggestion: If sortable tables appear in another feature, lift SortableMoveTable/COLUMNS into components/ui.tsx (or a components/tables.tsx) parameterized on the row type.

findings.issue: Card is one type serving three shapes — types? for the home grid, hidden? for ability pages — so consumers can't tell which fields are meaningful where; accreting more per-context fields will turn it into a flag bag.
findings.suggestion: Keep the optional fields for now, but if a third context-specific field appears, split into a base Card plus context-specific props passed by the page.

summary: This is an easy codebase to change: server data logic lives in one module, client components are dumb functions of typed view models, and the server-fn seam is current, idiomatic TanStack Start. Most cross-cutting rules (humanize, sprite URL, dashes, sort columns) have a single home, so typical fixes are one-file changes. The main editability cost is duplicated card construction between cardsFor and loadList, which makes display-rule fixes two-site changes and slightly softens removal and extension of the resource pages.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Deleting the route file is trivial and routeTree.gen.ts regenerates on build; typed Links make the compiler find the dangling references (pokemon.$name.tsx:78). But the Pokémon page's Abilities section, loadPokemon's abilities mapping, getAbility and the AbilityPage/abilities types each need their own edit, so it's five files — all small and greppable.

scenarios.change: Fix the card sprite for species whose default Pokémon has a different name (Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: All card rendering goes through PokemonCard (ui.tsx:31), which just renders card.sprite, so the fix is purely in the data layer. But the sprite is derived at two call sites — cardsFor (line 146, uses the Pokémon ref id) and loadList (line 172, uses the species id) — so one logical fix means two consistent edits in the same file, and forgetting loadList leaves the home page wrong.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: Every card list renders via CardList (ui.tsx:49), so sorting there covers move, ability and type pages in one edit. The trap: the home page paginates server-side (loadList slices at line 168), so sorting in CardList would only reorder within a page; a correct change needs the sort in loadList before the slice — two places with a subtle pagination pitfall.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: The moves.$name.tsx route file is a clean ~40-line template to copy, and the real substance is reusable: get/cardsFor/english/latestFlavorText/englishEffect helpers plus Section, Count, CardList, TypeBadge and orDash cover most of the page. Still no generic 'resource page' abstraction — loadItem is a new bespoke loader plus a new type and server fn, so it's four to five small files of template-following rather than plugging into an existing seam.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: apiBase() is the single definition of the base URL (line 24, env-driven, used by fetch and spriteUrl), and the entire cache — TTL constant (line 19), the Map, and the get() hit/eviction policy (lines 27-45) — sits at the top of one module. Nothing else in app/ knows where the data comes from.
